- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and model forecasts rise, reduce forecast by 1–4% to align with mean reversion tendency.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in first 5–7 days, assume momentum bias and adjust next 7–10 days downward.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges turning points; use 3-day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast adjustments.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.6) and price is trending, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days to catch momentum.
